data: Does the performance remain stable after the cutoff?

The figure shows an F-Measure learning curve for a TREC dataset using active learning with SVM and closest-to-hyperplane sampling. The training percentage is set to 10%, which is indicated by the purple line labeled "10% Training Cutoff." The blue stars represent measured performance points before the cutoff, while the red triangles represent measured performance points after the cutoff. The cyan line represents the Stabilizing Predictions (SP) method.

To determine if the performance remains stable after the cutoff, we need to observe the behavior of the performance points after the 10% training cutoff. The red triangles, which represent the performance points after the cutoff, align closely with the blue stars, indicating that the performance remains stable after the cutoff. Additionally, the cyan line, which represents the SP method, is also aligned with the performance points after the cutoff, further supporting the stability of performance.

Therefore, based on the visual analysis of the figure, the performance remains stable after the cutoff.
